- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen slope.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture downward trend in late period; add a 2–3% downward bias if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment momentum.
